newsitem.title: UK: CRICKET-AHMED CONTINUES TO DOMINATE SUSSEX BATSMEN.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-AHMED CONTINUES TO DOMINATE SUSSEX BATSMEN.

text.p: Pakistan leg-spinner Mushtaq Ahmed wrecked Sussex with a haul of six for 70 as they were dismissed for 241 by Somerset on the opening day of their county championship match on Wednesday.
It continued a remarkable run by the Pakistani who in his two previous county championship appearances against Sussex has finished with match figures of 12 for 175 and 10 for 116.
Ahmed took two wickets in the morning session and then after some defiant batting by Bill Athey (35) and Keith Newell (24) returned to take the last four wickets after tea.
Seamer Paul Jarvis responded for Sussex by trapping opener Mark Lathwell leg before and at the close Somerset were 35 for one.
Two former England test bowlers, Devon Malcolm and Phil DeFreitas, did their hopes of a recall no harm when they each took five wickets for Derbyshire against Middlesex at Lord's.
Fast bowler Malcolm finished with five for 50 and seamer DeFreitas five for 46 as Middlesex were dismissed for 146 after winning the toss.
Derbyshire then looked to be faring just as badly when they batted, rapidly being reduced to 23 for three with another former test bowler, Angus Fraser, taking two of them.
But by the close Derbyshire had recovered to 123 for five with Australian Dean Jones unbeaten on 42.

Worcestershire's Graeme Hick ended a lean spell by hitting his 91st first-class century and went on to make an undefeated 164. But it was against Oxford University and he will need a lot more runs against sterner opposition if he is to earn an England recall.
With Phil Weston making 119, Worcestershire declared at 359 for two. The university were 36 without loss at the close.
